field.tradition_name: Engineering, computing and the natural sciences

evidence.reason: some studies report samples or statistics, but no finding is firmly replicated

future_directions.title: Validation beyond the datasets used
future_directions.question: Do the frameworks and arguments put forward for Cyber Warfare hold up when tested against data?
future_directions.rationale: Phase 1 records validation beyond the datasets used as a limitation of Yang et al. (2025).
future_directions.next_step: Turn the proposed frameworks into hypotheses and test them on new, independently collected data
future_directions.feasibility_reason: fits a single study, using the design proposed in Phase 2

future_directions.title: Limited generalisability
future_directions.question: Which findings on Cyber Warfare hold beyond the settings in which they were first observed?
future_directions.rationale: Phase 1 records limited generalisability as a limitation of Sánchez et al. (2025).
future_directions.next_step: Repeat the strongest study's protocol in at least two new countries, sectors or populations
future_directions.feasibility_reason: requires partners or data access in each new setting

future_directions.title: Issues the studies leave open
future_directions.question: Which of the issues the reviewed studies leave open matters most for Cyber Warfare, and can a new study settle it?
future_directions.rationale: Phase 1 records these limitations: untested scalability (Yang et al. (2025)), limitations the authors acknowledge (Ahmed et al. (2024)), limitations the authors acknowledge (Li et al. (2024)), limitations the authors acknowledge (Lau et al. (2024)), limitations the authors acknowledge (Bouke et al. (2023)) and limitations the authors acknowledge (Kiely et al. (2023)).
future_directions.next_step: Design a focused study whose research question addresses this gap directly
future_directions.design: Mixed-methods design, as proposed in Phase 2
future_directions.feasibility_reason: depends on access to data on this gap

future_directions.title: Transparent reporting of effects and samples
future_directions.question: How large are the effects behind the findings on Cyber Warfare, and how precisely are they estimated?
future_directions.rationale: The abstracts of Sánchez et al. (2025), Yang et al. (2025), Fernandes et al. (2024), Celeny et al. (2024), Lau et al. (2024) and Li et al. (2023) give no effect sizes and sample sizes.
future_directions.next_step: Report the size of each improvement over the baselines with its variation across runs, and state the datasets' sizes

future_directions.title: Empirical tests of proposed frameworks
future_directions.question: Do the frameworks and arguments that rest on no new data stand up to testing?
future_directions.rationale: Yang et al. (2025), Diggelen et al. (2025), Ahmed et al. (2024), Huang et al. (2024), Li et al. (2024), Benkő et al. (2024), Ear et al. (2023), Bouke et al. (2023) and Kiely et al. (2023) collected no new data.
future_directions.next_step: Derive testable predictions from each framework and check them against independently collected data

future_directions.title: Reproducible evaluation
future_directions.question: Would the conclusions on Cyber Warfare change under the evaluation standards of engineering, computing and the natural sciences?
future_directions.rationale: Phase 2 places the reviewed studies in engineering, computing and the natural sciences, where work is judged above all on reproducibility and fair comparison with baselines.
future_directions.next_step: Report variance over repeated runs, compare against strong baselines on several datasets, run ablations and release the code
future_directions.feasibility_reason: needs compute time rather than new data

future_directions.title: Replication of single-study findings
future_directions.question: Which single-study findings survive an independent replication?
future_directions.rationale: The findings of Sánchez et al. (2025), Yang et al. (2025), Fernandes et al. (2024), Celeny et al. (2024), Lau et al. (2024) and Li et al. (2023) have not been reported by any other reviewed study.
future_directions.next_step: Repeat each study's design and measures on a new sample, reporting the result whatever its direction
future_directions.feasibility_reason: the original protocols define what to do

future_directions.title: Scaling up the evidence on challenges associated
future_directions.question: Does what is known about challenges associated hold at larger scale and in other settings?
future_directions.rationale: The evidence so far comes from India.
future_directions.next_step: Evaluate challenges associated at realistic scale: larger datasets, real deployment conditions and the hardware it would run on, reporting cost and latency as well as accuracy
future_directions.feasibility_reason: depends on compute and on partners for real deployments

future_directions.title: Collaboration with the social sciences and human-computer interaction
future_directions.question: What would the social sciences and human-computer interaction add to research on Cyber Warfare?
future_directions.rationale: The reviewed studies work within engineering, computing and the natural sciences; the social sciences and human-computer interaction would add a perspective they do not cover.
future_directions.next_step: Combine the field's own methods with user studies and stakeholder interviews on how the systems are adopted, trusted and governed
future_directions.feasibility_reason: depends on finding collaborators and a shared research question
